title: Tigrayan Tsebhi Birsen
community: Tigray people — the northernmost highland culture
author: Mama Tigist

heritage.origin: Tigray region — northern Ethiopia, the heartland of the Aksumite civilisation
heritage.history: Tigray is the northernmost highland region of Ethiopia — the heartland of the ancient Aksumite civilisation (1st—7th century CE) that was one of the world's first Christian kingdoms. Tigrayan cuisine (called Tigrinya cuisine) is closely related to Eritrean food and uses similar ingredients to the broader Ethiopian tradition but with distinctive preparation methods. Tsebhi (the Tigrinya word for wat) is made with more acidity (from tamarind or dried lemon) and a specific spice blend called Berbere Tigrinya that differs from standard berbere. Birsen means lentils — Tsebhi Birsen is the Tigrayan lentil wat.

desc: Tigrayan Tsebhi Birsen — red lentils cooked in the Tigrayan berbere-style sauce with a touch of dried lemon (left lemon) for acidity. The Tigrinya version of Misir Wat — more acidic, slightly different spice profile, representing the ancient northern food tradition.
longDesc: Tsebhi Birsen follows the same dry-caramelised onion technique as Misir Wat but uses the Tigrayan spice approach — a touch more acid, a specific blend that references the ancient Aksumite spice trade.
ingredients: 1 tbsp dried lemon rind (or 1 tsp tamarind paste)
steps: Add oil and berbere. Fry 3 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, dried lemon, and korerima.
Add lentils and water. Simmer 30—35 minutes.
chefTips: The dried lemon is the Tigrayan signature — it adds a citrus-tart note absent from standard Misir Wat.
Korerima is used in Tigrinya cooking more than elsewhere.
sustainabilityTips: Tigrayan lentils from the northern highlands.
culturalNote: Tigrayan food carries the weight of the Aksumite civilisation — the cuisine of the people who built the obelisks of Aksum, who received the Ark of the Covenant according to Ethiopian tradition, and who gave Ethiopia its first Christian church. Tsebhi Birsen is a lentil stew with 1,500 years of history.
